title: Establishing a multiplex imaging panel to study T cell development in the thymus in mouse
protocol: Fix and section tissues.
Incubate tissues in 4% Formaldehyde solution for 24 h.
Rinse tissue twice using 1× PBS by immersing tissue in plastic container full with PBS, then discard PBS and refill container with fresh PBS.
Put tissues in 70% Ethanol until embedding in paraffin blocks using standard protocols.
Dissect sections of 4 μm thickness and place on super-frost glass slide (Thermofisher).
De-wax slides by placing in 200 mL xylene for 10 min, then transfer the slides into another container with 200 mL of xylene for 10 min.
Place slides into 200 mL 100% Ethanol for 5 min, then transfer slides into a container with 200 mL of 100% EtOH for 5 min.
Place slides in 200 mL 70% Ethanol for 5 min.
Place slides back into distilled H2O.
Pre-heat AR buffer of choice (Sodium Citrate pH 6 or EDTA pH 9) for 1–2 minutes until boiling point.
Place slides in the pre-heated AR buffer and pressure cooker if using the pressure cooker method.
Remove slides from the pressure cooker and allow to cool down in AR buffer at approximately 20°C for 20–30 minutes.
Wash slides twice using dH2O after cooling.
Pre-heat water bath to 90°C before placing slides inside if using the water bath method.
Leave slides in a closed water bath with pre-heated AR buffer for 20 minutes.
Remove slides from water bath and allow to cool down in AR buffer at approximately 20°C for 20–30 minutes after water bath treatment.
Wash slides twice using dH2O after cooling.
Incubate slides for 20 min in 0.3% hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) buffer at approximately 20°C on a gentle rocker.
Wash slides twice with distilled water.
Draw around tissue carefully using Pap-pen (Abcam).
Add 5% serum of the host in which the secondary antibody was raised, enough to cover the entire tissue.
Incubate slides in a humidified dark chamber for 1 h at approximately 20°C on gentle rocker.
Place slide in TBST and incubate for 10 min at approximately 20°C with gentle rocking before adding primary antibody.
Avoid using Pap-pen on slides which were in TBST.
If slides were in TBST, wash thoroughly with dH2O before using Pap-pen.
Dilute primary antibody concentrations in 2% blocking serum in 1×TBS (1×TBS in dH2O).
Incubate tissues with primary antibody for 1 h at approximately 20°C or 18 h at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Wash 3× with TBST for 3 min while on a shaker.
Add immPRESS secondary antibodies (Vector Laboratories) on tissues and incubate for 1 h at approximately 20°C with gentle rocking.
Wash 3× with TBST for 3 min while on a shaker.
Mix DAB chromogen with tissues.
Incubate the mixture for 2–10 minutes at approximately 20°C with gentle shaking.
Wash the tissue twice in distilled water to stop the chromogenic reaction.
Incubate tissues in Hemotoxylin Solution for 20–30 seconds.
Wash tissues under running water for 3 minutes.
Incubate tissues in Scott’s buffer for 20–30 seconds.
Wash tissues under running water for 3 minutes.
Wash tissues once for 5 minutes in 70% alcohol.
Wash tissues twice for 5 minutes each in 100% ethanol.
Wash tissues twice for 10 minutes each in xylene.
Coverslip the slides with mounting media of choice.
Incubate tissues with primary antibody for 1 hour at approximately 20°C or 18 hours at 4°C with gentle rocking.
Wash tissues 3 times with TBST for 3 minutes while on a shaker.
Add secondary antibody as described in chromogenic detection optimization.
Prepare OPAL fluorophore staining buffer using fluorophore dilutions specified in Table 1.
Incubate tissue with OPAL buffer according to the incubation times indicated in Table 1.
Wash tissues 3 times with TBST for 5 minutes while on a shaker.
Wash tissues 2 times with dH2O for 2 minutes while on a shaker to remove excess TBST.
Incubate slides with DAPI (1 drop of spectral DAPI in 1.5 mL TBST) for 2–3 minutes, then wash 2 times for 2 minutes in dH2O.
Mount slides using anti-fading mounting media and cover the slides.
Incubate slides in a dark chamber at approximately 20°C for 18 hours.
Scan slides using Vectra 3 Automated Quantitative Pathology Imaging System.
Get tissue in focus then use autoexposure function to adjust exposure.
Optimal antibody dilution should have exposure between 60 ms and 120 ms.
Note optimal antibody dilution can vary between different OPAL fluorophores.
Optimize each antibody with different OPAL fluorophores when building a multiplex panel.
CD4 detection can be optimized using OPAL 520, 570, and 650 fluorophores.
This approach allows CD4 detection in different signal bands.
Identify how many heat cycles markers of interest can sustain before getting damaged.
Optimize heat cycle for each antibody as follows:
For AR Cycle 1: Perform regular staining steps from steps 3 to 8 with optimal dilution.
Scan stained slides.
For AR Cycles 2, 3, 4 and 5: Follow optimized heat cycle procedure.
Perform the regular staining step.
Add primary antibodies only in the AR cycle being tested.
Add secondary antibodies after adding primary antibodies as per the AR cycle.
Repeat steps 3 to 8 with optimal antibody dilution from previous trials.
Scan stained slides.
Identify optimal staining settings based on antibody concentration and exposure for each OPAL fluorophore.
Take a snapshot of optimized parameters using the Vectra machine.
Open the snapshot image in inForm software.
Extract signal spectral range from the snapshot image.
